To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of the GRB sample and other cosmological data makes the constraints on the ΛCDM and Cardassian models and several dark energy models more stringent, and that the dark energy equation-of-state parameter w(z) is constrained to be w(z) < 0.5 at 95% C.L. in the redshift interval z ~ 0-0.6.

(i) the GRB sample alone can not give stringent constraints on the cosmology and dark energy, (ii) the combination of the GRB sample with other probes can make the constraints more stringent and the best fit cosmology close to the ΛCDM model, (iii) the Cardassian expansion is also consistent with the data, (iv) two-parameter dark energy cosmology models are also consistent, and (v) we can constrain the dark energy equation and deceleration parameters

the combination of a recent GRB data sample, SNe Ia, CMB anisotropy and other cosmological data can provide strong evidence for the ΛCDMs model, and that the acceleration of the universe could have started at zt ~ 0.40-0.65.
